title: Bump the code-review.yml bot pin to match .relay/config.yml
body:
## Task

Set the `ref:` of the `Checkout code-review-bot (private)` step in `.github/workflows/code-review.yml` to the same `dvdtrsnk/code-review-bot` commit as `.relay/config.yml`'s `review.bot.ref`. When this issue was written that is `aa7d7e07f3bc3552887708a49dc319a3f4a2f640` (#547); if the Relay pin has moved since, use its current value.

Until this lands, the two pins differ on purpose. #547 bumped only `.relay/config.yml`, so Relay-run reviews use the line-number-free verdict-reuse identity (`dvdtrsnk/code-review-bot#28`), while reviews run by GitHub Actions still use `9e732e791c6bcdbfa4683d6ad93ed1f7441a3d61`. Those are human pushes and non-Relay pull requests. Meanwhile the "Relay delegation" step's comment in that workflow ("with the same pinned bot") is not true; once the pins match again it is, with no edit needed.

**When:** only after the choke-point-split batch (#494) has completed and no Relay implement branch is in flight. Any change under `.github/workflows/**` merged to `develop` makes GitHub reject the first push of every in-flight Relay implement branch. `.github/workflows/**` is also a protected path, so this is a maintainer change, not a Relay one.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `ref:` of `.github/workflows/code-review.yml`'s `dvdtrsnk/code-review-bot` checkout equals `.relay/config.yml`'s `review.bot.ref`.
- Nothing else in the repository changes.
- CI passes, including `code-review`, which runs under the new pin.

## Out of scope

- Any other change to the Relay or CI workflow configuration.
